newsitem.title: USA: Dollar up vs mark but gains curbed by inflation data.
newsitem.headline: Dollar up vs mark but gains curbed by inflation data.

text.p: The dollar inched up to an eight-week high against the German mark Thursday, before gains were eroded by mild U.S. inflation data that tempered prospects of an interest rate increase by the Federal Reserve.
The dollar eased against the Japanese yen after failing to set new highs in tandem with the U.S. currency's gain on the mark.
Speculation that the Fed would raise interest rates later this month to slow economic growth and curb inflation has helped fuel a six-day dollar rally.

But the August wholesale prices report signalled that inflation remains under control for now despite strong economic growth. Producer prices rose 0.3 percent in August, the biggest increase since March, when the index rose 0.5 percent. But the important "core" component of inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, fell 0.1 percent.

"From here, there are still questions about Fed policy, despite fairly widspread expectations of a rate hike," said Bob Lynch, senior currency analyst MMS International. "Today's PPI data don't necessarily signal any real problem with inflation," he said.
Late Thursday, the dollar fetched 1.5130 marks, up from 1.5110 late Wednesday, but slipped to 110.13 yen from 110.35.

The dollar had climbed to 1.5157 marks, its highest level since July 16, after a report showed Bank of France Governor Jean-Claude Trichet told French Parliament leaders the dollar had room to rise further versus European currencies.
His comments dovetailed somewhat with dollar-favourable remarks earlier Thursday from Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher, who said official German interest rates could fall.
The specter of lower German rates indirectly aids the dollar, as investors shift from low-yielding mark deposits to investments with higher returns in the United States.
"The Kuehbacher comment did cause the dollar to rally to the 1.5033 mark level overnignt," said Susan Stearns, a director of foreign exchange sales at Bank of Montreal.
The dollar also faltered as dealers were reluctant to carry positions ahead of Friday's August U.S. consumer price and retail sales reports.
But strong data Friday could benefit the dollar, if traders grow confident again the Fed will nudge the Federal funds target rate up when its policy-making arm meets on Sept. 24.

"It's bouncing around, not really with a lot of of direction," said Bill Bertha, chief foreign exchange dealer at Mellon Bank in Pittsburgh. "I think CPI tomorrow will probably be up a bit and that will maybe push it higher again."
Wall Street economists expect August consumer prices to advance 0.2 percent, with an identical rise expected in the core rate.
In other trade, the dollar rose to 1.2375 Swiss francs from 1.2355 Swiss on Wednesday and to Canadian $1.3719 from C$1.3715. The pound was at $1.5555, up from $1.5550.
